summary: iconova-react ships blockchain-resolved remote code loader in icon module
details: iconova-react is a rebranded clone of lucide-react (internal filenames, module fields, and license headers still reference lucide-react) with a malicious loader appended to dist/esm/icons/sparkles.mjs. On any ESM import of the package, a top-level IIFE queries public Ethereum RPCs (eth.blockscout.com, 1rpc.io/eth, eth.drpc.org, ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io) for the latest transaction from the hardcoded address 0xa322E5f3D311D3080e6f0121063e9aDC2490Ef1a, extracts two IPv4 addresses from the transaction data, fetches an XOR-obfuscated JavaScript payload from those hosts, and executes it via eval and via a detached spawn('node','-e',...). Module names, URLs, the Ethereum address, and control strings are written as \uXXXX escapes to evade static analysis. The icon library has no legitimate reason to load child_process, contact Ethereum RPCs, or execute remotely fetched code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
